question: When should I hire my first sales-enablement person?
answer:
**Hire your first sales-enablement person at $1.5M-$3M ARR with 4-6 quota-carrying AEs, when rep-to-rep variance in close rate exceeds 25 points and ramp time stretches past 5.3 months** (the cross-industry median per the [Bridge Group 2024 SDR Metrics & Compensation Report](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/reports), n=434 B2B sales orgs). Hire too early and you burn $145K+ on overhead with no playbook to systematize; hire too late and bad habits calcify across the team, costing 8-14 points of attainment that takes 9-18 months of remediation to recover. **Why these triggers (with primary-source numbers)** - **ARR floor of $1.5M:** Below this you cannot justify a fully-loaded $185K-$220K cost. The 2024 [Pavilion Compensation Benchmark Report](https://www.joinpavilion.com/comp-report) puts US Sales Enablement Manager median total comp at $148K (60th percentile $172K, 90th $215K), with a typical 70/30 base/variable split. Add 28% loaded burden (taxes, benefits, equity, tools) per the BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation [June 2024 release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.htm) and you land near $190K all-in. That is roughly 6-8% of ARR at $2.5M, which is the upper bound you should ever spend on a single non-revenue producer. - **AE count of 4-6:** Below 4 reps, the founder/VP can manually cross-pollinate best practices in 1:1s. At 4+ AEs, [Gartner's 2023 CSO survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/sales/insights) found close-rate variance climbs above 25 points without formal enablement, with the bottom-quartile rep contributing 11% of revenue while the top quartile contributes 47%. - **Ramp >5.3 months:** Bridge Group's 2024 dataset puts median full-productivity ramp at 5.3 months. Every month past that costs roughly the AE's monthly OTE quota in opportunity cost. For a $750K-quota AE, month 6 of slow ramp = $62.5K of unrecovered pipeline. - **Forrester / SiriusDecisions** has shown formal enablement programs lift quota attainment by 43 points relative to ad-hoc training (see their [B2B Sales Enablement framework](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/category/sales-enablement/), 2023 wave). **Six concrete pain signals (you need 3+ before hiring)** 1. **Variance test:** Top AE closes >35%, bottom AE closes <15% on similar ICP/lead source over a trailing 90-day window of 25+ closed-won/lost deals each. 2. **Onboarding test:** Last 2 hires took >6 months to hit 80% of quota (vs. the 5.3-month median). 3. **Playbook test:** Ask 3 reps to describe your discovery framework. If you get 3 different answers, you have no playbook. 4. **Repeat-question test:** The same tactical question (objection handling, MEDDPICC champion criteria, pricing carve-outs) gets re-asked in pipeline review more than twice in a quarter. 5. **Win-loss test:** You have not run a structured win-loss interview on the last 20 deals. Most founders cannot name the top 3 reasons they lost their last 10 opps. 6. **Tribal knowledge test:** If your top rep quit tomorrow, would her playbook walk out the door? If yes, you are running a single-point-of-failure system. **The right hire profile (with disqualifiers)** Look for: 3-5 years as a top-quartile AE (President's Club at least once, verifiable via W-2 or commission stub), followed by 1-2 years owning at least one enablement workstream (onboarding curriculum, call coaching cadence, or competitive battlecard library). Bonus if they have shipped a [Gong](https://www.gong.io/)/Chorus call-scoring rubric or a MEDDPICC/SPICED implementation. References describe them with the words "systems," "frameworks," or "data" — not "motivational" or "high-energy." Hard disqualifiers: failed AE who never hit quota (will rationalize away rep skill gaps), career trainer with no carrying-quota background (cannot earn rep trust), pure content marketer (will produce decks no one uses), or anyone whose 30-day plan is "a kickoff offsite." See [/knowledge/q12](https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/q12) for the parallel framework on hiring the first RevOps person and [/knowledge/q07](https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/q07) on building hiring scorecards that actually predict performance. **Comp structure that aligns incentives** Pay $115K-$135K base + $35K-$50K variable. Variable splits 60% to **team quota attainment**, 25% to **ramp time of the next AE hire**, and 15% to **content adoption** (% of reps using the new playbook in Gong-recorded calls). The 70/30 base/variable split mirrors the Pavilion 2024 dataset and avoids the most common failure mode: enablement person becoming a glorified pipeline-management coach who steals deals. **First 90 days (concrete deliverables)** - **Days 1-14 — Audit:** review 60 days of Gong/Chorus calls for top-2 and bottom-2 reps. Output a 12-15 page "observed playbook" memo (actual, not aspirational). - **Days 15-30 — Win-loss:** conduct 15 structured interviews (10 won, 5 lost). Output: top-3 win drivers and top-3 loss drivers, with quote-level evidence. - **Days 31-60 — Framework build:** ship one canonical discovery framework (MEDDPICC, SPICED, or Command of the Message — pick one), one objection-handling library covering the top 8 objections, and one demo storyline. Get explicit buy-in from the top AE first; she is your distribution channel. - **Days 61-90 — Onboard next AE:** instrument every milestone (week 2 product cert, week 4 mock pitch, week 6 first discovery, week 8 first close). Target: 80% quota by week 20 vs. the prior baseline. See [/knowledge/q31](https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/q31) for the full new-AE ramp scorecard. **Six-month KPIs** - Time-to-productivity for new AEs: <5 months (down from 6+). - Close-rate variance across reps: <12 points std dev (down from 25+). - Win rate on deals using the new framework: +6 to +9 points vs. ad-hoc deals. - Onboarding NPS from new hires: >50. - % of deals with MEDDPICC fields populated at Stage 3+: >80%. If three or more of these are not moving in the right direction by month 6, you hired the wrong person — cut at month 7 and re-hire. If three or more of these KPIs are not moving in the right direction by month 6, you hired the wrong person; cut at month 7 and re-hire. See [/knowledge/q18](https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/q18) for the underperformer-management framework. **Bear Case (the genuinely adversarial counter-argument)** The honest case against hiring enablement at $1.5M-$3M ARR is not just "too expensive." It is structural: 1. **Selection bias in the success stories.** Most case studies showing enablement ROI come from companies at $10M+ ARR with 15+ reps. At 4-6 reps, your sample size is too small for any framework to prove statistical lift inside 6 months. You may be paying $190K to *believe* you have a system rather than to *have* one. Honest counter: enablement at this stage is partly an option on future scale, not a guaranteed in-period ROI. 2. **The VP of Sales should already be doing this.** If you have a competent VP Sales (which at 4-6 AEs you should), playbook design *is their job*. Hiring an enablement layer can mask a weak VP and let them off the hook for the strategic work. Ask yourself: would firing the VP and hiring a stronger one solve more than adding a layer underneath? 3. **Fractional first is sometimes correct.** A $7K-$12K/month fractional enablement consultant for 6 months ($42K-$72K) can build the same framework with less burden, and you keep the option to hire full-time once you have 8+ reps. See [/knowledge/q42](https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/q42) for the fractional-vs-full-time decision tree. 4. **Reps reject top-down playbooks.** [Forrester's 2023 sales enablement study](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/category/sales-enablement/) found 67% of enablement content goes unused. If your culture is "reps build their own approach," a heavy-handed enablement hire will trigger rebellion and your top rep may quit. The fix is hiring someone whose first 30 days are listening, not lecturing — but most candidates are wired the opposite way. 5. **Cash math at <$3M ARR is unforgiving.** $190K loaded cost at 75% gross margins requires roughly $253K of incremental ARR from enablement to break even in year 1. If your blended ACV is $30K, that is 8.4 net-new logos directly attributable to enablement work — almost impossible to prove cleanly inside 12 months. The honest answer: hire enablement when you cannot scale your sales motion without it, not because the calendar says so. If you are at $2M ARR with a strong VP Sales who is shipping playbooks weekly and your variance is <15 points, *wait*.
